long_biography.plain_text:
Perfect pitch gave Frayda B. Lindemann an early path into music. She studied piano as a child and earned a music degree at Hunter College. In her thirties, she returned to Columbia and completed a doctorate in musicology. She then taught at Hunter.

Her work moved from scholarship to arts governance. Lindemann joined the Metropolitan Opera board, directed her giving toward young singers and helped endow the program that bears the family name. She later chaired OPERA America and served as president and chief executive of the Met's board. She is now president emerita and a managing director. The resources behind that philanthropy came from businesses built by her late husband, not from the nonprofit institutions she led.
